- Reduce noisy Android log output and centralize runtime logs to a file for easier diagnostics on device.

author: adityakk9031
body:
Fixes #305055

Summary
When moving the pointer from a through-going sash toward a T-junction, the sash briefly loses its hover highlight before both sashes light up. This is a directional bug: moving in from the terminating sash does not exhibit the issue.

Root cause: Sash.onMouseLeave removed the hover CSS class synchronously. When the pointer crossed into the orthogonal drag handle overlay, the browser fired mouseleave on the through-going sash first. By the time mouseenter fired on the orthogonal handle, the hover state was already gone, causing a visible flash before the delayed hoverDelayer re-added it.

Change
src/vs/base/browser/ui/sash/sash.ts
 — Sash.onMouseLeave

diff
- sash.el.classList.remove('hover');
+ sash.hoverDelayer.trigger(() => sash.el.classList.remove('hover'), 0).then(undefined, () => { });
The removal is now scheduled through the same hoverDelayer instance used by 
onMouseEnter
. Because both enter and leave share the delayer, a synchronously-following mouseenter on the drag handle will cancel the pending removal — keeping the hover class on the element with no visible flicker.

💡 **What:**
Wrapped the synchronous file reading logic (`open().read()`) within an inner helper function (`_read_file`) and executed it using `await asyncio.to_thread(_read_file)`. 

🎯 **Why:**
The current `fetch_remote_file` method contained synchronous I/O. File reads on local disk can block the asynchronous event loop, degrading the backend's concurrency capabilities, especially under heavy load. The issue was well-isolated and replacing it with a non-blocking asyncio thread execution was straightforward and safe.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
Conducted a concurrency-based micro-benchmark (reading 100 2.2MB dummy files simultaneously alongside an event loop heartbeat task).
- **Baseline:** `Total time: 2.6935s`, `Average event loop delay: 0.0439s`
- **Optimized:** `Total time: 1.1580s`, `Average event loop delay: 0.0131s`
- **Result:** ~57% reduction in total time for massive concurrent reads, with a massive ~70% drop in event loop delay, directly demonstrating the event loop is far less blocked by file I/O operations.

## Summary

- Adds `benchmark/benchmark_glm_xgb_cnn.R`, a native R reimplementation of the Python benchmark
- **GLM**: `glmnet` multinomial ridge regression (alpha=0, default lambda path, maxit=5000)
- **XGBoost**: `xgboost` R package (200 rounds, depth 6, hist tree method)
- **CNN**: Custom implementation using Rcpp-compiled im2col/maxpool kernels + mini-batch SGD in R (R torch unavailable — no network access to download the lantern backend)

## Results

| Model | Test Accuracy | Train Time |
|-------|-------------|------------|
| GLM (glmnet ridge) | 81.30% | ~470s |
| XGBoost | 89.84% | ~179s |
| CNN (Rcpp conv, SGD) | **90.09%** | ~706s |

## Key implementation details

- **Rcpp kernels**: `im2col`, `col2im`, `maxpool_fwd`, `maxpool_bwd` compiled at runtime via `sourceCpp`, parallelised with OpenMP
- **OpenBLAS**: Used for fast matrix multiplication in conv layers
- **NCHW layout**: All tensors stored as flat vectors; reshape via `aperm()` (no R-level loops)
- **Bug fixed**: `as.double(matrix)` in R is column-major — input images must be transposed first (`t()`) to get the row-major NCHW layout expected by im2col

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `Rscript benchmark/benchmark_glm_xgb_cnn.R` from the repo root
- [ ] Confirm GLM, XGBoost, and CNN results print with accuracy and train time
- [ ] Verify CNN epoch losses decrease (epoch 1 ~0.58 → epoch 10 ~0.22)

author: sjhddh
body:
Fixes #1393 and #1000.

Currently, the native `SummarizationMiddleware` replaces the conversation history in `state["messages"]` with a generated summary plus a trailing window of messages. This permanently erases the original history from LangGraph checkpoints, causing the frontend to render truncated dialogue histories upon page refresh.

This patch introduces a `SafeSummarizationMiddleware` wrapper that hijacks `SummarizationMiddleware.abefore_model`. Instead of returning a destructive state update with `RemoveMessage(id=REMOVE_ALL_MESSAGES)`, it captures the summarized window and injects it directly into the `ModelRequest.messages` via `awrap_model_call`. 

This ensures that the token reduction strictly applies to the current inference window passed to the LLM, while leaving the authoritative `state["messages"]` and DB checkpoints completely intact and immutable.

body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
## Purpose
Related to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/2194

The proper fix for the above issue is to merge the sampling params to get the correct `num_inference_steps`, but this PR adds a short-term workaround for teacache, which doesn't depend on `num_inference_steps`. It also adds logging if the cache fails to reset for now while I am working on the more general fix.

This is needed because the warmup initializes teacache, which replaces forward(), and can cause bad behaviors when running TTI on models that accept image inputs. E.g., for Flux2Klein

```python
from vllm_omni import Omni
from vllm_omni.inputs.data import OmniDiffusionSamplingParams

if __name__ == "__main__":
    omni = Omni(
        model="black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B",
        cache_backend="tea_cache",
    )

    prompt = "A cat sitting on a windowsill"

   # If you specify num_inference_steps, you will see the second cache refresh (after warmup)
   # but if you don't pass it, you won't since refresh won't be called.
    sampling_params = OmniDiffusionSamplingParams(
        # Not specifying num_inference_steps will crash forward
    )

    outputs = omni.generate(prompt, sampling_params)
    outputs[0].images[0].save("meow.png")
```

Not refreshing before entering the forward pass will blow up because the new modulated inputs don't have an image component, while the previous (stale) ones do.
```
ERROR 03-26 18:11:45 [diffusion_worker.py:481]   File "/home/alex-jw-brooks/vllm-omni/vllm_omni/diffusion/cache/teacache/hook.py", line 222, in _should_compute_full_transformer
ERROR 03-26 18:11:45 [diffusion_worker.py:481]     (modulated_inp - state.previous_modulated_input).abs().mean()
ERROR 03-26 18:11:45 [diffusion_worker.py:481]      ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
ERROR 03-26 18:11:45 [diffusion_worker.py:481] RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (4096) must match the size of tensor b (8192) at non-singleton dimension 1
...
ERROR 03-26 18:11:45 [stage_diffusion_client.py:78]   File "/home/alex-jw-brooks/vllm-omni/vllm_omni/entrypoints/async_omni_diffusion.py", line 309, in generate
ERROR 03-26 18:11:45 [stage_diffusion_client.py:78]     raise RuntimeError(f"Diffusion generation failed: {e}") from e
ERROR 03-26 18:11:45 [stage_diffusion_client.py:78] RuntimeError: Diffusion generation failed: The size of tensor a (4096) must match the size of tensor b (8192) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

This PR allows teacache to refresh in this case, and adds a log if we can't refresh the cache while the more correct fix is added.

@Gaohan123 @wtomin @fhfuih could you please take a look?

body:
## Summary

Improve scan-all workflow resilience for transient scanner failures.

## Problem

When the scanner app returns a transient 503 (e.g., during cold start after deployment), the HTML error page gets written to the `.sarif` file. The SARIF upload step (`if: always()`) then tries to parse this HTML as JSON, causing: `Invalid SARIF. JSON syntax error: Unexpected token '<'`

## Fix

- **Retry logic:** Scan retries up to 3 times with 30s backoff between attempts
- **Guarded SARIF upload:** `upload-sarif` only runs when `steps.scan.outputs.scan_ok == 'true'` instead of `always()`
- Artifact upload still runs on `always()` for debugging failed scans

Fixes [AB#2111](https://dev.azure.com/MngEnvMCAP675646/ec743f54-ae41-40e5-9630-58235cb009f7/_workitems/edit/2111)
